name: deviation_from_ema_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index deviates sharply from its 5-minute EMA — reflected as a z-score exceeding ±1.5 standard deviations of recent deviations — VWAP-benchmarked execution algorithms and market makers begin absorbing the overshoot. These participants are accumulating at prices well better than their benchmark, creating a floor (or ceiling) that arrests the drift and initiates a micro snap-back. At 5-second resolution we detect the first bar where the deviation z-score peaks and reverses (narrowing), signalling that fresh counter-directional orders have entered the book. The ATM CE or PE captures the initial 30-90 second reversion leg before the EMA is reached.

indicators.name: ema_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute EMA as the rubber-band anchor. The original used EMA(50) on 1-min = 50-minute anchor, which is too slow for a 15-90 second hold. We compress to 5 minutes (60 bars at 5s) — long enough to define the local micro-trend NIFTY is deviating from, short enough to respond to the fast intraday moves we're trading. The key is detecting deviations from the RECENT local trend, not the full session trend.

indicators.name: dev
indicators.purpose: Raw deviation from 5-minute EMA in NIFTY index points. Forms the basis for z-score normalization.

indicators.name: dev_zscore
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling z-score of deviation. The 120-bar (10-min) window normalizes current deviation against recent volatility regime — a 10-point NIFTY deviation is extreme in a calm session but unremarkable on a high-VIX day. Replaces the original ATR(14) normalization; z-score is more robust on the index because ATR at 5s resolution is extremely noisy. NOT a blind 12x scale of original's ATR(14): the original used 14-min ATR as a cross-sectional stock volatility normalizer, while we need a session-volatility normalizer for the index.

indicators.name: snap_confirmation
indicators.purpose: Checks that the z-score peak has passed and reversion has begun. Direct port of original's 'ema_dev_atr[t] > ema_dev_atr[t-1]' confirmation. Uses 2-bar lag instead of 1-bar to reduce single-bar noise at 5s resolution.

conditions: dev_zscore[t] > dev_zscore[t-2] (deviation starting to narrow — snap-back initiated)
VIX < 25 (avoid extreme fear regimes where mean reversion fails)
in_session (09:30-15:20 IST — need 15 min warmup for EMA + rolling std)
buy_ce.confirmation: Two consecutive bars of z-score improvement (current > 2 bars ago) confirms snap-back is real, not noise

conditions: dev_zscore[t] < dev_zscore[t-2] (deviation starting to narrow — fade initiated)
buy_pe.confirmation: Z-score beginning to compress from peak confirms overhead sellers have entered

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points. If NIFTY continues 8+ pts further from EMA after our entry, the snap-back thesis is broken and we're in a momentum continuation move, not a rubber-band reversion. At delta ~0.5, 8 spot pts = 4 option pts. This aligns with the 1-minute typical NIFTY move of 3-7 option pts — our stop is right at the edge of the 'normal' zone.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points of reversion toward EMA. The median micro-snap on NIFTY from a ±1.5σ EMA deviation covers 60-70% of the deviation, typically 10-15 spot points. At delta ~0.5, 12 spot pts = 6 option pts. Targeting 6 captures the first leg without chasing the full reversion (which takes longer than our 90s max hold). R:R = 1:1.5.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 25 — above 25, NIFTY mean reversion is unreliable as trending panic overrides the rubber-band dynamic
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — skip first 15 min to allow EMA(60) and rolling std(120) to warm up with valid data
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume at 5s is too noisy for meaningful thresholding
filters.trend_filter: implicit via EMA slope: dev_zscore only fires extreme signals when EMA is near-flat; strong trending markets produce fewer but less reliable signals
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — EMA rubber-band is a well-known concept; the z-score normalization + snap-back confirmation add a layer of specificity. Most algos fade at fixed-point or ATR thresholds, not rolling z-scores, which provides differentiation.

adaptation_notes: Original used EMA(50)/ATR(14) on 1-min bars of NIFTY200 stocks (50-min anchor, 14-min ATR). Three key changes: (1) EMA period compressed from 50-min to 5-min — we're catching the micro rubber-band, not the session rubber-band; (2) ATR normalization replaced by rolling z-score — ATR on 5s bars is too noisy for index data, z-score normalizes against current session volatility regime; (3) Entry filtered to VIX<25 rather than VIX<25 (same, but explicit in code). Hold time compressed from 10-30 min to 15-90 seconds — we enter exactly when the snap-back begins, not after a 1-min bar confirms. The snap-back confirmation (deviation narrowing on consecutive bars) is preserved directly from the original.
weaknesses: EMA(60)=5min may be too reactive on high-volatility NIFTY sessions — the 'rubber band' may stretch further before snapping, triggering stops
Rolling z-score over 120 bars uses only 10 minutes of history — regime shifts mid-session can cause the std normalization to misprice the threshold
During index futures expiry sessions, NIFTY micro-deviations from EMA can persist as pin risk dominates over mean reversion
Signal frequency depends heavily on market volatility — very low-VIX sessions may produce few or no signals
